ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), as amended; Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA) including the online investment-linked financing chapter; Act on Protection of Personal Information; FSC Regulation on Financial Institution Supervision; and KOFIU administrative guidance incorporating FATF recommendations. Korean beneficial ownership records are centralized under the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) and disclosure to the public is not permitted; competent authorities and obligated financial institutions access UBO data under strict law-enforcement and AML/CFT supervision.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Company Registration (Certified Corporate Registry Extract, Korean: Beob-in Deung-gi Sa-hang Jeon-bu Jeung-myeong-seo)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, competent District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at a Korean notary public; if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) must issue a Hague Apostille. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, do not apostille; instead, complete MOFA consular authentication followed by legalization at the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. The two paths are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Tax Payment (Korean: Nap-se Jeung-myeong-seo)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at a Korean notary public; if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, obtain a Hague Apostille from MOFA. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, obtain MOFA consular authentication and then consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Articles of Incorporation (Korean: Jeong-gwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public and/or the competent District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certified copy at a Korean notary public; for Apostille Convention destination states, attach a MOFA-issued Hague Apostille. For non-Apostille destination states, use MOFA consular authentication and destination-embassy consular legalization in Seoul; never use both apostille and consular legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing company formation, UBO disclosure, and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / General Meeting of Members of the entity, with Korean notarization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized resolution is first executed before a Korean notary. If the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, the notarized document must receive a MOFA Hague Apostille. If the receiving jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, the notarized document must receive MOFA consular authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. Use only the applicable path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean licensed commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank branch or head-office banking team maintaining the corporate escrow or operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The issuing bank's authorized officer must execute the reference letter, then it must be notarized by a Korean notary. For Apostille Convention destination states, the notarized letter receives a MOFA Hague Apostille. For non-Apostille destination states, the notarized letter receives MOFA consular authentication and destination-embassy consular legalization in Seoul. The apostille and consular paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any founder, director, shareholder, UBO, or crowdfunding issuer, the platform must perform real-time screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK consolidated list, KOFIU domestic watchlists, and the Financial Services Commission designation of high-risk jurisdictions. All UBOs and controlling officers must be screened using exact, phonetic, partial, and fuzzy matching, including alias, former-name, and passport-number variants. Foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence with documented source of wealth and source of funds. Continuous transaction monitoring is mandatory over ACH escrow and bank-wire rails, including currency transaction threshold reporting and suspicious transaction reporting to KOFIU within three business days; negative media and adverse legal events trigger immediate enhanced review, account restriction, or closure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-Net (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (https://www.iros.go.kr) together with the National Tax Service Hometax Business Registration portal and the competent District Court Registration Office for the entity's principal place of business
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the registered trade name must be written in Hangeul. A foreign-language name may appear in parentheses or as a secondary transliterated name, but the controlling legal name must be in Hangeul with the legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa (Korean: Yuhan Hoesa). The four-tier naming convention is: exclusive distinctive identifier + business purpose/industry + optional geographical indicator + legal-form suffix. English names must be transliterated phonetically and accurately into Hangeul; Hanja characters may be used only where commonly accepted, and Hangeul remains decisive for registration, court, tax, and payment-platform records.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crowdfunding (unless the online investment-linked financing license has been granted)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant must obtain a written rejection stating the grounds under the Commercial Act. Within 14 days from rejection, the applicant may file a written objection with the Head of the competent District Court Registration Office, attaching a revised name, prior name-search report, board resolution, and statutory justification. If the Registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may petition for administrative review through the Court Administration Office and subsequently file an administrative lawsuit in the competent administrative court within 90 days. Counsel should also clear conflicting trademarks with the Korean Intellectual Property Office and FSC naming restrictions before refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this regulated equity crowdfunding portal. The Financial Services Commission online investment-linked financing license requires a physical, staffed office in Korea at the registered address; that office must be disclosed to KOFIU and the National Tax Service and must store board minutes, AML/CFT policies, customer due diligence files, audit trails, server logs, and accounting books. The tax office will reject an address that is only a mail-forwarding service, and banks will refuse to issue the mandatory bank reference letter or open the escrow accounts for a virtual-office entity. A fully compliant serviced office with long-term lease, physical signage, private meeting rooms, and 24-hour file accessibility is the minimum acceptable structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70-85% probability within the first 12 months after license application or grant. Inspection checklist: lease registration certificate, physical signage and door plate, on-site compliance officer and staff, local servers or authorized cloud logs, board minutes, AML/CFT manual, customer due diligence files, UBO records, suspicious transaction reports, business continuity plans, telecom and data-processor agreements, accounting records, and IT security controls. Inspecting agencies include the Financial Services Commission, KOFIU, the National Tax Service, and the Seoul Metropolitan Government or other competent municipal tax office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (as amended), Articles 543-569, governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company); Commercial Registration Act, Articles 4, 15-23; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, Articles 117-10 through 117-26 for online small investment broker (equity crowdfunding portal) authorization; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 8 for non-resident capital remittance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; online filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) and StartBiz portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, accompanied by authenticated Articles of Incorporation and statutory attestation schedules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under Korean company law; contribution may be nominal KRW amount and no blocked escrow is required by the Commercial Act. The registry requires a bank certificate evidencing deposit. Separately, the equity crowdfunding portal authorization under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act imposes prudential capital, surety bond and FSC licensing requirements before regulated activities commence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (THE 'COMPANY'), ADOPTED ON [DATE], AT THE COMPANY'S REGISTERED OFFICE IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF ALL DIRECTORS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMMERCIAL ACT AND THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. THE BOARD RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS. 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS. The Board examines the subscription schedule and accepts the paid-in capital amount of KRW [amount] contributed by the members. The Board ratifies each contribution, confirms that each subscriber has agreed to acquire a membership interest, and directs the Representative Director to record all contributions in the capital ledger and to issue contribution certificates. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts the registered office at [address], Republic of Korea, as the Company's legal seat and directs the Representative Director to execute the lease, obtain landlord registration consent, and file the address with the Registry Court, National Tax Service and any relevant financial regulator. 3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Auditor, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall serve until the close of the next annual meeting of members. The Representative Director is vested with full executive authority; the Auditor supervises legal and financial compliance; the Corporate Secretary maintains minute books and statutory records. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the Representative Director, jointly with the Corporate Secretary or another signatory approved by the Board, to open, manage and close bank and escrow accounts, including ACH escrow and bank wire accounts, to sign mandate forms and to approve electronic payments. 5. REGULATORY AND LICENSING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to apply for the online small investment broker/equity crowdfunding portal authorization before the Financial Services Commission, to engage legal counsel, certified public accountants and tax agents, and to sign all documents required to implement the Company's licensed crowdfunding business. 6. RATIFICATION. Any actions taken by the Representative Director with respect to the above matters before the date of these resolutions are ratified and confirmed. These resolutions are effective immediately and shall continue in force until amended or revoked by the Board or by a higher corporate authority. This instrument is the official pro-forma record of the First Board Resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) and StartBiz national business commencement portal; with jurisdictional Registry Office of the district court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search for the proposed corporate name 'Yuhan Hoesa' in the IRO database to ensure it is not identical or confusingly similar to a previously registered Korean entity. Confirm that the proposed registered office is a physical address within the territorial jurisdiction and obtain the certified copy of the lease agreement or certificate of ownership together with written landlord consent confirming that the premises may be used as the registered seat of the company. If any member is a non-resident, record the country of residence, passport identity, and intended capital remittance route to prepare the foreign-exchange filings required at the investment stage.
required_dossiers: Name search result or name reservation confirmation from IRO/StartBiz
Proposed corporate name in English and Korean transliteration (Roman script)
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for proposed registered office
Landlord written consent for corporate registration
Passports/government IDs of all founding members and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the office location is queried, file a revised name application with an alternative distinguishable corporate name and submit a corrected landlord consent with a clearer premises identification. If the registry retains the suspension, use the online IRO helpdesk and the jurisdictional registry clerk to obtain the written defect reason, then re-file within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Subscription Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding members and a Korean notary public (beopmusa) licensed in the Republic of Korea; review by a Korean corporate attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean and in a certified English translation, containing all mandatory statutory particulars: trade name, corporate purpose, registered office, total paid-in capital, number and class of contribution units, valuation of non-cash contributions, method of contribution, names and addresses of members, officers and auditor, term, accounting period, and corporate governance provisions. Each founding member must sign or seal every page. Where non-cash contributions are used, obtain an in-kind contribution appraisal report and attach it to the subscription schedule. Notarize the articles before a notary public to facilitate bank onboarding, registry acceptance, and Financial Services Commission licensing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Korean original and English translation)
Subscription schedule listing member names, nationalities, residential addresses, contribution amounts
Certified passports or resident registration cards of all members
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Power of attorney, if a representative acts for the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry model detects defects, execute a conformed amendment deed and re-notarize only the corrected pages. If an in-kind valuation is disputed, substitute cash contribution by a supplementary member resolution and re-issue the subscription schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Bank Certificate of Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea; for non-residents, a Foreign Exchange Bank and Bank of Korea reporting window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a designated pre-registration deposit account at a licensed Korean bank in the name of the company under incorporation, with the founding members as authorized signatories. Cable or deposit the paid-in capital into the account and instruct the bank to issue a certificate of paid-in capital deposit setting out the depositor, company name, account number, deposit date, and final balance. Ensure the bank marks the deposit as restricted for paid-in capital and not withdrawable except after incorporation registration. For non-resident members, submit the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act report through the dealing bank before funds are remitted, and ensure the remitter name precisely matches the member name in the Articles of Incorporation and subscription schedule.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Company name reservation certificate
Foreign exchange declaration form for non-resident investment
Passports/IDs of the authorized founders opening the account
Proof of source of funds and beneficial ownership for AML/KYC clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account or blocks the deposit due to AML/KYC deficiencies, provide supplemental source-of-funds documentation and an organizational chart of beneficial owners through the bank compliance office. Where the bank requires a financial license for the crowdfunding purpose, request that the account be designated solely as an incorporation escrow account pending FSC licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registry Filing for Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company to the jurisdictional Registry Office, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate proving paid-in capital deposit, written acceptances of the Representative Director and Auditor, landlord consent, foreign exchange declaration evidence for non-resident members, power of attorney if filed by an agent, and proof of payment of court filing fees and capital registration tax. The registry clerk verifies statutory compliance, assigns a corporate registration number, and issues a certificate of registered incorporation. This registration creates the legal personality of the Yuhan Hoesa and must be completed within the statutory filing window after execution of the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company
Authenticated/notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by bank
Written acceptance forms signed by the officers and auditor
Landlord consent and lease registration documents
Foreign exchange investment report and tax payment receipts
Power of attorney and filing checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspension or deficiency notice, obtain the written defect statement from the registration clerk, execute a corrective addendum under the Commercial Registration Act, pay any additional registration tax or stamp duty, and re-submit the complete package through IRO. If the defective filing cannot be cured, withdraw the application and file a new one before the statutory expiration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Statutory Post-Incorporation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the Hometax portal and local district tax office; Korean Employment and Labor Office for payroll; Financial Services Commission for crowdfunding licensing follow-up.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation registration is certified, obtain the corporate seal certificate and apply for a Korean business registration certificate from the National Tax Service using Hometax or StartBiz. Complete the registration for corporate tax, value-added tax if applicable, employment insurance, national pension, and withholding tax for officers and employees. Affix the company seal to statutory forms and open a commercial bank account in the company name using the registered corporate certificate. File an immediate updated foreign-investment declaration if non-resident shareholders exist, and initiate or continue the Financial Services Commission online small investment broker licensing application with the certified incorporation certificate and audited financial documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration from the Registry Court
Company seal certificate
Business registration application form (NTS Form)
Lease agreement and landlord consent
Corporate officer appointments and ID copies
Foreign investment declaration and licensing framework for crowdfunding portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS requests an on-site inspection, schedule a physical inspection, have signage and lease custody available, and present the original lease contract. If the FSC licensing is delayed by missing corporate attestations, provide the certified envelope of the Registry and notarized officers' acceptance, and request a pre-licensing consultation with the FSC Capital Market Supervision Division.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC), Capital Market Division; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for regulatory examination; if physical office facilities are operated, the relevant municipal district office is responsible for ordinary building administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Online Small Investment Broker Registration (Equity Crowdfunding Portal) under Article 117-13 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; industrial manufacturing, assembly or warehouse operating permits are Not Applicable for ISIC 6499 digital intermediary.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment consultation is not required because the registered activity is an office-based digital crowdfunding intermediary with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Environmental Impact Assessment and Environmental Registration are not required; only standard municipal waste collection and wastewater connection charges apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None generated - zero regulated wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste handling in the ordinary course. If future office fit-out or server room installation creates backup generator emissions, the operator must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act emission concentration limits and noise standards set by the Ministerial Enforcement Rule, and a simple Environmental Registration may become necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for Civil Defense fire permits for factory/chemical occupancy. The office operation requires an ordinary fire safety inspection under the Fire Services Act for the leased office floor, structural load clearance if server racks are installed, and workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for the staff of a licensed online investment-linked financing portal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; principal digital platform: HomeTax (Hometax.go.kr), with customs-related export clearances performed through UNI-PASS (Korea Customs Service)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa, and for a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean taxable supply: (1) complete Korean commercial registration; if the entity is non-resident, first appoint a domestic tax representative or place of business representative; (2) assemble apostilled or certified foreign articles, corporate registry excerpt, board resolution, and power of attorney; (3) submit the Business Registration Application to the district NTS office having jurisdiction over the Korean registered address; file within 20 days of business commencement; (4) obtain the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number (serving as the VAT ID and TIN) and confirm activation of HomeTax e-tax invoice credentials; (5) for non-resident owned entities, preserve the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting receipts for share capital and escrowed crowdfunding funds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for Yuhan Hoesa or hybrid mismatch elections. The entity is taxed as a domestic corporation on worldwide income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) - national indirect tax, not a GST or US-style sales-and-use tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for Korean corporate taxpayers; a Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT from business commencement. The simplified taxpayer turnover threshold (KRW 80 million) applies only to individual businesses and cannot be used by a limited liability company or any foreign non-resident VAT registrant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory under the Value-Added Tax Act. Each tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS via the HomeTax e-invoice system by the statutory deadline (generally the 10th day of the month following issuance); no real-time transactional fiscal clearance and no anti-fraud digital stamp is used. NTS operates API-based submission through HomeTax and detects fraud by cross-matching purchase and sale tax invoices and by the mandatory issuance of e-tax invoices for all VAT-creditable transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods and services supplied and consumed outside Korea are zero-rated. For an equity crowdfunding portal, qualifying cross-border digital intermediary services provided to non-resident issuers and investors are zero-rated when the place of supply is outside Korea, the service is not used for a domestic establishment, and the Korean supplier receives foreign-currency consideration through foreign exchange repatriation to Korea. Services connected to domestic Korean startups or Korean resident users remain standard-rated at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (UNI-PASS export declaration and clearance certificate, the functional equivalent of a Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Commercial Invoice and service agreement for cross-border digital intermediary services
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank
Non-resident status evidence of the overseas recipient (e.g., foreign corporate registry excerpt or passport and vendor due-diligence file)
Place-of-consumption substantiation for digital services (e.g., subscriber IP logs, user location records, contractual governing-law and place-of-use terms)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service audit export files and can disallow zero-rating if physical export, foreign consumption, or foreign-currency settlement is not proven within 180 days or with valid documentation. Clawback is retrospective: the full 10% VAT is assessed with statutory interest plus additional tax for under-reporting and non-declaration; fraudulent documents or deliberate evasion trigger criminal prosecution under the Act on Regulation of Tax Offenses and liabilities of responsible officers of the Yuhan Hoesa.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating in tandem with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the Foreign Exchange Authority and supported by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but precisely monitored convertibility regime. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, current transactions such as trade settlement, royalties, fees, and dividends are generally freely convertible through registered foreign exchange banks, subject to submission of underlying transaction evidence and foreign exchange reporting forms. Capital account transactions are not fully unrestricted; they are governed by a positive-list approach where market participants obtain approvals, declarations, or notifications depending on the transaction type. Foreign direct investment into a Korean entity enjoys a streamlined notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and effectively requires conversion at a domestic FX bank with proper investor identification. Profit remittances by foreign shareholders are permissible under current-account rules, but a Korean withholding tax, normally 20% plus local surtax unless reduced by tax treaty, must be settled via the local bank; the bank requires board resolutions, audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and evidence of paid-in capital to ensure the remittance is not a disguised capital flight. Export proceeds must be received in foreign currency through an FX bank, converted immediately if the exporter has no matching won obligations, and declared through the Foreign Exchange Information System. In sum, capital controls remain layered, bank-mediated, and surveillance-heavy, not market-totalitarian.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export claims must be settled as prescribed by Korea's Foreign Exchange Regulations. An exporter must deliver the export proceeds through a domestic foreign exchange bank and may be required to sell or deposit the foreign currency within 30 days from the due date or expected receipt date. The statutory settlement period for export receivables is generally within 1 year of the export date; longer terms require advance approval. In practice, when export proceeds are collected, if the bank account is a won account with automatic conversion, the won amount is credited immediately; if kept in foreign currency, the proceeds count as a foreign currency deposit and conversion is not mandatory if they will be used for future foreign currency payments. For follow-on compliance, exporters must file the export declaration through Korea Customs Service and the bank subsequently reports the settlement through the Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW / NOT VIABLE AS STANDALONE. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, or Currenxie cannot open local clearing accounts in Korea in their own name as third-party EMIs unless they obtain an FSC e-settlement license or partner with a licensed banking institution under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. The Korean entity may receive remittances from foreign EMIs only if those EMIs route through an intermediary or licensed bank; however, using them as the primary clearing rail is untenable because they are not treated as domestic foreign exchange banks and cannot facilitate Korean cash-management products, won settlement, or statutory tax and FX filings. Domestic Tier-1 banks must be used for the platform's cash custody and FX rails; EMIs may be used only as last-mile collection for small foreign investors and with full traceability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, a physical presence or equivalent supervised authentication is mandatory. For a foreign-invested Korean LLC, the statutory representative or director should physically attend a branch of the designated FX bank. Non-face-to-face account opening is possible using accredited initial attestation by a Korean notary or via video interview with the bank's compliance officer, but the bank may demand an overseas notarized corporate registration, apostilled by the Korean consulate or notarized locally, plus cross-verification of passport data. Remote consular proxy opening generally is not independently sufficient as a full KYC interview; a video interview with a bank officer who performs live verification of the statutory identity and signature remains the practical standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the legal entity chain and beneficial ownership of the Korean LLC, where the crowdfunding platform receives multiple minority shareholder injections from overseas individuals; any mismatch in the registry or nominee-shareholder arrangement creates an enhanced due diligence event.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified copies of Certificate of Corporate Registration, Articles of Incorporation, consolidated UBO table, shareholding ledger and register of members, individual ID and passport copies, proof of residential address for each shareholder, completed bank beneficial ownership disclosure form, and, where nominee arrangements are disclosed, formal nominee agreement and underlying trust deed plus a legal opinion confirming no shell-company restrictions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital escrow and investment monies passing through the portal; crowdfunding refund flows can resemble money laundering layering when inbound investor wires are pooled and then moved to disbursement wallets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of all funding accounts for 24 months, investor-side bank statements or proof of bank card ownership, signed escrow deed and rules of the crowdfunding platform, detailed ledger mapping each investor contribution to a specific offering, anti-money laundering policy, transactional monitoring procedure, audit report from a licensed Korean CPA for escrow balances, and a third-party independent fund-flow opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory licensing and suspicious transaction reporting triggers; because ISIC 6499 covers financial service activities, the entity must hold an equity crowdfunding license or authorization under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, and the bank may block onboarding if the license is not yet issued or if it lacks a registered AML compliance officer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the FSC license or provisional authorization, business continuity plan, AML manual, nomination of the AML compliance officer with resume, international sanctions screening policy, data protection impact statement, litigation disclosure, confirmation that the platform is not operating as an unauthorized payment processor under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and evidence of cooperation with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political exposure and jurisdictional overlap with high-risk countries while accepting investor deposits from abroad; the bulk of foreign investor remittances from jurisdictions with weak AML regimes triggers extra scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geographic risk matrix, sanctions screening screenshots for each investor and counterparty, negative news alerts, source-of-wealth certification for each investor above USD 50,000, escalation dossier with explanation of any prior bank suspicion reports, and a written legal undertaking to restrict access to sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections are processed as foreign direct investment through a domestic foreign exchange bank. The Korean LLC must file an FDI notification with the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy or Invest KOREA before remittance or within the statutory filing window. The foreign investor wires funds to the dedicated Foreign Investment Account or ordinary current account of the LLC using SWIFT MT103, clearly quoting the FDI notification number and the bank-compliant foreign exchange purpose code. On receipt, the bank verifies the notification number, value of remittance, and investor identity; the LLC then completes foreign currency verification and capital tax treatment. Funds are credited to the company's corporate account in KRW or foreign currency. For escrow traffic connected with crowdfunding, maintain a separate custody account with a signed custody agreement, and obtain an external capital confirmation report or bank certificate of paid-in capital for statutory settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: KRW trade disbursements are cleared via domestic banking rails through the Bank of Korea processing infrastructure; cross-border trade settlement uses SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for transfers, commercial letters of credit for import financing, and documentary collections with documents against payment or documents against acceptance for trust-based trade. To avoid FX remittance refusals, ensure underlying trade contract, commercial invoice, bill of lading, Korea Customs Service export or import declaration, and foreign exchange transaction forms are prepared. For outbound dividends or royalties, the paying bank requires tax receipts, withholding tax proof, board resolution, and audited financials. Platform operational disbursements to investors or refunds must be kept in the domestic escrow and ACH loop unless they are related to an underlying trade or service obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with an underlying exposure and tenors linked to actual export or import dates, executed through a Korean domestic FX bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; speculative hedging without underlying documentation is prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards on USD/KRW may be entered into by qualified Korean corporates only for real commercial exposure and must be documented, with physical delivery preferred; currency swaps are allowed for two-currency liability matching, subject to a risk-management form filed with the bank.

Derivatives for hedging KRW operational capital are limited further to spot transactions and simple swaps; any option trades require prior approval and must be identified in the bank's derivative product evaluation and suitability system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; within three months of the approved fiscal year-end for any other fiscal year, inclusive of lawful extension periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing add-on tax of 20% of corporate tax due; simple underreporting add-on of 10%; fraudulent or aggravated underreporting add-on of 40%; statutory overdue interest until full settlement; tax liens, compulsory seizure and collection; for a licensed crowdfunding portal, persistent tax delinquency is treated as a fitness-and-propriety failure and may trigger FSC license revocation as the administrative forfeiture trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government tax office of the relevant Si, Gun, or Gu within the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; within three months of the approved fiscal year-end for any other fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local Tax Act nonpayment additional tax of 10% of unpaid local corporate income tax; compulsory local tax collection and asset attachment; denial or non-renewal of local tax clearance certificates required for FSCMA crowdfunding portal license renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Return for January-June Taxable Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 25 of the same year for the January-June taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, failure to file or false filing attracts add-on taxes of 10% for underreporting, 20% for non-filing, and 10% for neglect; input tax credits may be disallowed; repeated violations support criminal referral and administrative scrutiny of the crowdfunding license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Return for July-December Taxable Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 25 of the immediately following year for the July-December taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, failure to file or false filing attracts add-on taxes of 10% for underreporting, 20% for non-filing, and 10% for neglect; input tax credits may be disallowed; repeated violations support criminal referral and administrative scrutiny of the crowdfunding license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report for Registered Online Investment-Linked Finance Equity Crowdfunding Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission of the Republic of Korea and Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false filing may result in administrative fines, corrective orders, suspension of crowdfunding solicitation, license revocation, and criminal penalties under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; license revocation constitutes the administrative forfeiture of the portal's operating permission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and AML Compliance Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Annual Business Report no later than March 31; any material beneficial-ownership change must be reported within 30 days of the triggering transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of beneficial-ownership and AML reporting obligations may attract administrative fines, supervisory sanctions, criminal liability, and revocation of the crowdfunding portal license where the entity is found to be controlled by an unapproved or unfit beneficial owner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Members and Statutory Register Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office, independent external auditor, and Commercial Registration Court on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the close of each fiscal year and in any event before the corporate income tax filing deadline; register updates are available on demand to NTS and FSS upon supervisory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary meeting or to maintain statutory registers renders financial statements incapable of lawful member approval; Korean Commercial Act administrative fines may be imposed on directors or managers and the FSC may treat continued noncompliance as a supervisory deficiency affecting license fitness.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC) operating as a licensed equity crowdfunding portal is compulsorily subject to an independent certified public accountant audit if: (a) it is an online investment-linked finance or equity crowdfunding portal registered under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, regardless of size; (b) it is a financial investment business entity whose license condition requires audited financial statements supporting the annual business report; (c) its total assets at the prior fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500,000); (d) it exceeds any two of the following Presidential Decree thresholds: total assets of KRW 7,000,000,000, annual revenue of KRW 20,000,000,000, or 100 full-time employees; or (e) the Financial Services Commission or Financial Supervisory Service determines that a High-Risk AML tier crowdfunding portal requires an external audit in the public interest despite being below all monetary thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) for non-public non-financial general companies; Korean SME Accounting Standards for qualifying small and medium-sized entities; all audited financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and accompanied by an audit report issued by a CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The portal must maintain a real-name beneficial ownership control file under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specified Financial Transaction Information and the FSCMA license conditions. An annual UBO confirmation must be submitted to the Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit together with the Annual Business Report no later than March 31. Any issuance, transfer, pledge, or other disposition of capital contribution units or any change in beneficial ownership or control must be recorded in the Register of Members and reported to the competent Commercial Registration Court and, for the licensed portal, to the FSC and KoFIU within 30 days of the triggering event. The 30-day window is mandatory and cannot be extended, and the annual confirmation does not supersede the transaction-specific reporting obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Capital Contribution Units
Register of Directors / Executives and Management Officers
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Encumbrances
Minute Book of General Meetings of Members and Management Resolutions
Register of Beneficial Owners and AML Customer Due Diligence File

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a professional corporate secretarial agent and virtual registered-office arrangement in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 28,000 per annum for a K-IFRS compliant certified independent CPA audit of a regulated crowdfunding portal

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax; aggregate top effective rate 26.4% including the 10% local income tax surtax (lower brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% up to KRW 20 billion; 21% up to KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea grants R&D expense/equipment tax credits, venture-business income tax deductions, Free Economic Zone/Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays, and SME tax reduction incentives; no general patent box regime applies to a crowdfunding portal, but a qualified foreign investor locating in an FEZ may obtain a 5-year corporate tax holiday with a 2-year 50% reduction, subject to statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return (CTA Article 60) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing system; the return is the principal annual corporate income tax return for Yuhan Hoesa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations must also make preliminary quarterly corporate tax prepayments on estimated taxable income, but the comprehensive return is filed once for each fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the close of the fiscal year (e.g., a December 31 fiscal year-end return is due by March 31 of the following year), unless an extension is obtained for consolidated financial statements or an external audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business year gross income and operating loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all Korean-source and worldwide income of the Korean entity; for a resident LLC, non-resident shareholders' equity income is not entered here, and cross-border income from the crowdfunding portal must be separated from investment transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: non-deductible expenses, depreciation adjustments, reserve reversals, and intercompany/transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter arm's-length adjustments for all cross-border related-party service, licensing, cloud, and crowdfunding platform fees; attach specified TP documentation if the aggregate overseas related-party transaction threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (tax base) after deduction of carried-forward tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the correct loss carryforward deduction (10 years, limited to 80% of taxable income for non-SMEs except where SME rules apply); ensure non-resident-related expenses are not deducted if excessive under thin capitalization or earnings-stripping rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate tax using progressive national rates plus local surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%/19%/21%/24% brackets and add 10% local income tax; report foreign tax credits only for taxes paid to foreign states that satisfy DTA conditions; no credit is available for withholding tax on non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign shareholder and non-resident beneficiary declarations, dividends paid, and treaty relief adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the foreign ownership schedule for every non-resident shareholder showing country of tax residence, Tax Identification Number, ownership percentage, and entitlement to DTA benefits; retain Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedules and mandated foreign transactions report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit the statement of foreign-currency/foreign-related transactions, cross-border intercompany contracts, Limitation-on-Benefits declarations, and any equity crowdfunding escrow/settlement account details requested by the National Tax Service.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an unpaid-tax negligence penalty of up to 20% of the assessable tax plus daily late-payment surcharges; under-reporting or refund abuse adds a 10%-40% penalty; deliberately filing a false corporate return is criminally prosecuted under the Tax Offense Punishment Act with imprisonment or fines up to twice the evaded amount, and directors are exposed to secondary collection under National Tax Collection Act Article 39.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate domestic statutory withholding on outbound dividends to non-resident corporate shareholders (20% corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax); treaty relief may reduce the rate to 5%-15% depending on ownership and the applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for reduced DTA rates, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the foreign tax authority, complete the payer-side tax treaty exemption application in HomeTax, demonstrate beneficial ownership and no abuse under any Limitation-on-Benefits clause, and submit the documents to the Korean payer before payment; any incorrectly withheld excess can be reclaimed through a statutory tax treaty refund claim within the applicable prescription period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding is 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax) for non-resident interest and royalties; most Korean tax treaties reduce interest to roughly 10%, industrial/commercial royalties to 10%-15%, and copyright royalties to 10% or 15%, subject to beneficial ownership and LOB substantiation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for the fiscal year exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is required when the multinational group has consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion; different or simplified thresholds may apply to small entities and CbC reporters.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Caribbean-style ESR, but applies statutory substance-over-form rules under the Corporate Tax Act and beneficial-ownership requirements under tax treaties; the equity crowdfunding portal must keep its core income-generating activities (issuer due diligence, KYC/AML, escrow settlement, investor communication, board oversight) onshore in Korea with locally employed directors/managers and physical records, otherwise the National Tax Service may disregard the Korean entity for treaty/TP purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unregistered financial investment business / crowdfunding license violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal and collecting investor funds without registering as an online crowdfunding intermediary with the Financial Services Commission, or soliciting startup equity investments outside the statutory limitations of the FSCMA regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FSCMA Article 444: imprisonment up to 3 years or a criminal fine up to KRW 100 million; the FSC may issue cease-and-desist orders, revoke registration, and impose administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face individual criminal imprisonment/fines, civil joint and several liability to reimburse misappropriated crowdfunding proceeds, FSC blacklisting and travel bans, and personal asset seizure upon court order when the corporate veil is pierced for fraud or willful misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion, false non-resident declarations, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating deductions for offshore management or platform fees, hiding the true beneficial owner behind nominee foreign shareholders, falsely claiming treaty reduced withholding, or understating Korean-source crowdfunding commissions in the annual corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Offense Punishment Act Article 9: imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to twice the evaded corporate tax; additional 10%-40% tax penalties under CTA Article 76; aggravated sentencing for large-scale evasion under the Act on Aggravated Punishment for Specific Economic Crimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: National Tax Collection Act Article 39 authorizes collection from directors who intentionally or grossly neglect their duties when corporate assets are insufficient; directors may also face civil restitution, travel blacklisting by the Ministry of Justice, and criminal imprisonment that can substantially exceed the base 2-year term if the evaded amount is large.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CDD failure and false suspicious-transaction reporting for crowdfunding escrow flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence on non-resident investors, allowing anonymous beneficial owners to fund issuers through the platform, and failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit for escrow or wire transfers connected to sanctioned entities, fraud rings, or shell-company nominees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Article 4 suspicious transaction reporting duty and related penalty provisions) can produce criminal fines up to KRW 50 million or imprisonment up to 5 years, along with FSC license revocation and disgorgement orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, civil damages for investor losses, a prohibition on re-entering financial services, travel bans/blacklisting, and piercing of the Yuhan Hoesa veil in cases of deliberate AML compliance failure or knowing participation in money laundering.
